title: Simplified mole negro with chicken

ingredients.note: bone-in pieces, poached in water with onion and salt, broth reserved
a mix of mulato, pasilla and guajillo, stemmed and seeded

steps: Poach the chicken with onion and salt until just cooked. Keep the chicken warm and reserve about 1.5 l of the broth.
Toast the chiles briefly on a dry pan until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 20 minutes. Take care not to burn them, which makes the sauce bitter.
Toast the almonds, peanuts, sesame, spices and raisins separately in a dry pan. Fry the plantain and char the tortillas until black.
Blend everything with the drained chiles and about 500 ml of broth until completely smooth, in batches.
Heat the oil in a wide pot until hot and add the paste. It will spit. Fry, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Add the chocolate and enough broth to loosen, then simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring often. Season with salt, and add a little sugar if it tastes harsh.
Add the chicken to the sauce and warm through. Serve with rice or tortillas.
notes: This is a shortcut version. Authentic Oaxacan mole uses chilhuacle negro chiles and a longer list of ingredients, and may take a full day.

title: Oven cochinita pibil

ingredients.note: juice, or 120 ml orange juice mixed with 80 ml lime juice
sliced and pickled in lime juice with salt and habanero

steps: Blend the achiote, sour orange juice, garlic, cumin, oregano, allspice and 2 tsp salt into a smooth marinade.
Coat the pork in the marinade, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Heat the oven to 160 C. Line a baking dish with the banana leaves, add the pork and juices, and fold the leaves over to wrap.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for about 4 hours, until the pork is very tender and shreds easily.
Shred the meat in its juices and serve in warm corn tortillas with the pickled onion.
notes: Banana leaves are sold frozen in Latin and Asian shops. Baking parchment and foil work if you cannot find them, with less aroma.

title: Chiles en nogada

ingredients.note: roasted, peeled, with a slit and seeds removed
fresh if possible, peeled and soaked in milk overnight

steps: Roast the chiles over a flame until blistered, steam in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel. Slit down one side and remove the seeds without tearing the chile.
Fry the onion and garlic in oil, add the pork and brown it. Add the tomato and cook until the sauce has reduced.
Add the peach, apple, raisins, almonds, cinnamon and salt, and cook for 15 minutes until the fruit is soft and the mixture holds together.
Blend the walnuts with the cream, queso fresco and sherry until smooth. Add a pinch of salt.
Stuff each chile with filling and press the slit closed. Warm them in a low oven for 10 minutes.
Spoon the cold walnut sauce over the chiles, scatter with pomegranate seeds and parsley, and serve.
notes: The sauce is traditionally served cool and the chiles room-temperature or warm. Contains tree nuts.

title: Red snapper a la veracruzana
steps: Season the fish with salt and lime juice and leave for 15 minutes.
Heat the olive oil and cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaves and oregano and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Stir in the olives, capers and jalapeños with a splash of water.
Place the fish in the sauce, spoon sauce over the top, cover and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes.
Serve with white rice.

title: Pan de muerto
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, anise and zest. Add the warm milk, 3 eggs and orange blossom water and mix to a dough.
Knead in the butter a little at a time until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1.5 hours.

Take off a quarter of the dough. Shape the rest into 8 rounds, and from the reserved dough make bone-shaped strips and a small ball for each loaf. Lay the strips across the top and set the ball in the middle.
Rest for 45 minutes. Heat the oven to 180 C. Brush with beaten egg and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden.
Brush the hot loaves with melted butter and roll or dust them in sugar.

title: Red pork tamales in corn husks

ingredients.note: dried, soaked in hot water until pliable
or vegetable shortening, at room temperature

steps: Put the pork, onion, half the garlic and 1 tsp salt in a pot, cover with water and simmer for 1.5 hours until tender. Shred the meat and keep about 700 ml of the broth.

Toast the chiles briefly on a dry pan, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes. Blend with the remaining garlic, cumin, a pinch of salt and about 150 ml of the soaking water until smooth, and strain.
Fry the chile sauce in a spoonful of the lard for 5 minutes, add the shredded pork and simmer until thick and not watery. Season and cool.

Beat the rest of the lard for 3 minutes until fluffy. Mix the masa harina, baking powder and 1 tsp salt together, then add to the lard in portions with the warm broth until you have a soft, spreadable dough. Season generously, as steaming dulls the flavour.

Drain the husks and pat dry. Spread 3 tbsp of dough in a thin square over the wide end of a husk, leaving a border. Put a spoonful of filling in the middle, fold the sides over and fold up the narrow end.
Stand the tamales upright, open end up, in a steamer lined with spare husks. Cover tightly and steam for 60 to 75 minutes, topping up the water as needed.
A tamale is done when the dough pulls away cleanly from the husk. Rest for 15 minutes before serving.
notes: Banana leaves can replace the husks for a different, moister style. Tamales freeze well and reheat by steaming.

title: Pozole rojo with pork

ingredients.note: shoulder on the bone, cut into large pieces
cooked, canned or jarred, drained and rinsed
guajillo and ancho, stemmed and seeded
from about 3 limes, or serve as wedges

steps: Cover the pork with 3 l of cold water in a large pot with the onion, 3 cloves of garlic, bay leaves and 1 tbsp salt. Bring to a simmer, skim off foam, and cook gently for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Toast the chiles on a dry pan for under a minute until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 20 minutes.
Blend the chiles with the remaining garlic, oregano, cumin and about 250 ml of the soaking water until smooth. Strain into the pot.
Add the hominy and simmer another 45 to 60 minutes. Remove the pork bones, shred the meat roughly and return it.
Taste and adjust the salt. The broth should be rich and slightly thick.
Serve in deep bowls with the cabbage, radish, lime and more oregano on the table for each person to add.
notes: Dried hominy (maiz cacahuazintle) gives the best texture but needs overnight soaking and 2 to 3 hours of cooking.

title: Oven tacos al pastor

ingredients.note: boneless shoulder, sliced about 5 mm thick

steps: Blend the soaked chiles, achiote, the pineapple for the marinade, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano and 2 tsp salt until smooth.
Coat the pork slices in the marinade, cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 240 C with a rack in the upper third. Thread the slices onto skewers or stack them tightly on a rack over a tray so the edges can crisp.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred and the pork is cooked through.
Chop the pork finely. Pile it onto warm tortillas and top with diced pineapple, onion, coriander and lime.
Serve at once with a red or green salsa.
notes: A vertical spit gives the traditional shaved texture. The oven method trades that for convenience, so use high heat and thin slices to get crisp edges.

title: Vegetarian tlayuda

ingredients.note: large corn tortillas, 25 cm or bigger; or double-layered small ones
cooked, with a little of their cooking liquid
shredded or pulled into strands; mozzarella works
guajillo or pasilla, toasted and soaked, blended into a salsa with 1 clove garlic and lime

steps: Fry the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the beans and mash with a little cooking liquid to a spreadable paste. Season with salt.
Toast each tortilla directly on a hot griddle or grill pan for 2 to 3 minutes per side until dry and slightly crisp but still foldable.
Spread the bean paste over each tortilla, leaving a rim.
Scatter over the cheese and return to the heat for a minute or two until it starts to melt.
Top with the cabbage, avocado, tomato and salsa. Fold in half or serve open.
notes: For a traditional version add grilled cecina (thin salted beef), tasajo or chorizo. Authentic bean paste is often made with lard.

title: Esquites in a cup

ingredients.note: kernels, fresh cut from about 4 cobs or thawed frozen
a few leaves, optional; or use coriander
pure ground chile, not a spice mix

steps: Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat and cook the onion and chilli for 2 minutes.
Add the corn, a pinch of salt and the epazote if using. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the kernels are tender and just starting to brown.
Spoon the warm corn into cups with a little of the pan juices.
Top each with mayonnaise, crumbled cheese, a squeeze of lime and chile powder, and eat with a spoon.
notes: Use a splash of water if the pan dries out. Some cooks use stock instead of water, but water keeps it vegetarian.
